member.name: RefinePreciseMarkAsync
member.para: Why the correction is not ground truth. Die Dritte Macht chapter 7 is the case on record (2026-07-31, see ): the heuristic mark this method exists to correct was 0.04 s off, and the correction moved it 1.16 s early.

The removed cheap first round. There used to be one ahead of the search, sampling at VAD speech-segment starts within a jingle-plus-phrase span of the mark, from the days when the search was a fixed-step sweep costing hundreds of transcriptions. Removed 2026-07-30 after the BARDIOC.m4b log settled it: over 26 refinements it confirmed 3 times, spent 606 checks and 8.1 minutes doing it, and the search then closed all 23 of the remaining marks in 3.8 minutes. It could not be repaired either, for a structural reason worth recording. Its window was fixed-width, so shifting it moved both ends and "is the phrase heard here" was not a step function - it could only ever be sampled at guessed positions, never searched. The one guess that mattered, the announcement's own VAD speech start, lands past the onset by VAD's onset lag (0.60 s measured on Perry Rhodan "Die Dritte Macht" chapter 4, true onset 4142.572 s vs. a VAD start of 4143.168 s, 2026-07-30; ~0.4 s recorded earlier by tools\vadprobe's precise prototype), i.e. on the far side of the plateau edge where confirmation depends on Whisper recovering a clipped first syllable. Nothing inside the plateau was ever a candidate, because only segment starts were collected and never the pauses between them. Widening its window would not have helped: the wider it got, the less "the phrase is the first thing heard" implied "the phrase starts near here". Anchoring the window's end instead, which is what makes the search monotone and bisectable, is the only fix - and that is the search this method now runs.

What the upgrade-model retry measured. On the two marks that prompted it (2026-08-02, chapters 6 and 14 of one German audiobook, -m small -M turbo): the single probe that broke each search read "* Musik *" on the small model and "Kapitel 6 Fernweh 3" respectively "Kapitel 14 Srimavo" on the upgrade one, and every foothold the corrected edge would then have offered confirms on it.
How often the failure branch is reached. Over a ten-book run only five marks of 271 reached it at all, and a refinement is a handful of short decodes - which is what makes the second pass affordable.

What the fallback is worth. Keeping the heuristic mark was validated against a real audiobook's full set of known good and previously-broken marks (see tools\vadprobe's precise prototype) before this was ported here. The default-mode heuristic it falls back to measured within 0.05-0.35 s of the true onset for 25 of BARDIOC.m4b's 26 marks, so the fallback is a fraction of a second of accuracy rather than a broken mark.

member.name: AnchorOnsetToSoundAsync
member.para: How closely sound follows the silence end. Measured over the fourteen-book run of 2026-08-03 (114 marks with a silence in reach, each one's audio decoded and measured): the sound really does start within 0.1 s of the silence end 113 times, and once - Paula Monti chapter 19, a -47 dBFS click at 3:18:50.72 with the word "Première" not beginning until 3:18:51.13 - it starts 0.39 s later. That single case is why the silence end is treated as a floor to walk forward from rather than as the onset itself.

How often the no-floor jingle branch is taken. Replaying PrecedingSilenceEnd over the corpus's own logged silences and onsets, 264 of 440 refined marks reach it; 60 % of a book's marks is typical, and BARDIOC, Das Mutantenkorps, Die Maahks and Gruelfin reach it with every mark they have. Books without jingles (I Shall Wear Midnight, Paula Monti, The Forever War) never do. Before covered that branch such a mark kept the raw plateau edge, which is how "Stalker.m4b" chapter 24 came to sit 0.12 s later in one build than another for no better reason than a changed probe window.

member.name: LocatePhraseByShrinkingWindowAsync
member.para: The rejected fixed-step sweep. Stepping at a time across the span cost up to 2 x span / step transcriptions - 726 of them, some twenty minutes, on the mark that prompted the rewrite (Stalker.m4b's "Zeittafel", 2026-07-29).

The anchored-end predicate, verified before it was built. On that same mark: starts of 22.6, 30, 40, 46, 50, 51.5, 52 and 52.5 s all still found "Zeittafel" against an end of 54 s, and 53 s did not - one edge, no island.

How much headroom the search ceiling has. Measured against the ten-book run of 2026-08-02 (222 refinements that reported an onset), the onset landed past the ceiling exactly twice, by 1.4 s and 2.2 s, with a median headroom of 6.9 s - so one of reach covers every case on record with room to spare.

The one refinement that ever aimed from the ceiling. Raumschiff Erde chapter 1, the case this was built for and the only one of 278 to reach the branch: its detecting decode was a 26.7 s overlap tail from 0:04:55.38 and Whisper timestamped "Kapitel 1." as its very first segment, 0.0-7.0, twelve seconds before the words were spoken, so the bracket [0:04:42.38, 0:05:07.38] ended right at the announcement rather than behind it. The words are in fact at 0:05:07.0-0:05:12.0 and the onset at 307.50 s, the plateau's last confirming probe being 307.60 and the first failing one 307.70 (tools\wprobe, ggml-small, 2026-08-02); a foothold probe at the ceiling, 307.38, confirms cleanly and the walk from it lands on exactly that onset.

member.name: FindPhraseSurvivalEdgeAsync
member.para: What a fixed-width bracket did to the predicate. Measured twice while this was built, both on Stalker.m4b's "Zeittafel" (true onset 52.7 s, 2026-07-29): anchored 55 s out, the phrase was reported surviving from 22.92 s but not from 23.32 s and the edge came back 29 s early; anchored at the detecting window's end but started from the mark 30 s before it, the very first stride straddled a chunk boundary and did it again. Bracketing to the matched segment made the same audio behave perfectly monotonically.
